abstract: Maintains tropospheric transmission metrics, water vapor telemetry, and cloud cover records
system_message:
You are the Atmospheric sciences lead (ATM). Your business responsibility is maintaining tropospheric transmission metrics, water vapor telemetry, cloud cover records, and surface microclimate monitoring logs for candidate observatory sites.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains tropospheric transmission metrics, water vapor telemetry, and cloud cover records（ATMO）
information_points.content:
ATM-ATMO-MT1：For Atacama Chajnantor High Plateau, precipitable water vapor continuous monitoring is verified via an active calibrated submillimeter zenith radiometer installed at the candidate peak. Across annual observation nights over the summit, the median precipitable water vapor column depth above the receiver horizon is 750 um.
ATM-ATMO-E9D：For Sierra Negra Volcanic Saddle, precipitable water vapor continuous monitoring is verified with an active calibrated zenith radiometer on the candidate peak. Annual observation nights show a median precipitable water vapor column depth of 1700 um above the receiver horizon.
ATM-ATMO-D60：For Pico Teide Caldera Ridge, precipitable water vapor continuous monitoring is verified by an active calibrated zenith radiometer at the candidate peak. During annual observation nights over the summit, the median precipitable water vapor column depth above the receiver horizon is 750 um.

information_points.title: Surface microclimate monitoring（WIND）
information_points.content:
ATM-WIND-YT8：For Pico Teide Caldera Ridge, continuous 24-month summit weather station recordings document an annual maximum wind gust speed of 110 km/h at telescope elevation.
ATM-WIND-39A：For Sierra Negra Volcanic Saddle, continuous 24-month summit weather station recordings record an annual maximum wind gust speed of 140 km/h at telescope elevation.
ATM-WIND-BM5：For Atacama Chajnantor High Plateau, continuous 24-month summit weather station recordings measure an annual maximum wind gust speed of 175 km/h at telescope elevation.
